note: Built around the two classic voices, Coupé Cloué's Trio Select (1970s) and the Jacmel troubadour Ti Paris, then the revival: Mizik Mizik's Blakawout, the Haiti Twoubadou project's acoustic versions of compas hits (Pa Manyen Fanm Nan, Ma Rose, Ou Pati, Tu me touches), Haitiando's Kreyòl versions of Cuban songs, and later guitar groups (Lole-Lolay, Gifrants, New York Twoubadou). Map di is Coupé Cloué's larger Ensemble Sélect, at the compas edge. Ti Paris and most Haiti Twoubadou tracks carry only reissue dates, so their years are left null.

size.basis: A judgement written before collecting, not a count; no source counts recordings. Twoubadou lives mostly as live music in small clubs, restaurants, hotels and patron-saint feasts, so much of it was never recorded. What is on record: the songs of Kandjo (Auguste de Pradines) and other early singers; the guitar-band albums of the 1950s-1980s on Haitian and New York diaspora labels (Ti Paris, Coupé Cloué's Ensemble Select with dozens of LPs, Trio Select, Toto Nécessité, Ti-Coca and similar small groups); and the commercial revival from the late 1990s (the Haitiando series, the Haiti Twoubadou compilations, Mizik Mizik's Blakawout), plus a stream of local CDs and online singles. Diaspora LPs are poorly catalogued. An insider's essential list is about 35 recordings, many of them Coupé Cloué, Ti Paris and the revival compilations.
